Subject: Production degradation impacting Mesher - urgent

Sergio —

We saw a sustained degradation yesterday and overnight that materially affected requests routed to us-west-2. Symptoms: p95 latency spiked to ~2.1s (baseline ~300ms), 5xx rate increased from 0.1% to ~3.4% for a ~5-hour window, and effective throughput dropped to ~40% of our committed baseline. This hit several customer-facing flows and we have churn risk with two large end-customers.

Attached is a snapshot (mesher_incident_snapshot.zip) with request ids, timestamps, and tracerids. Please escalate — we need an executive-level remediation and an ask for commercial credit while we assess customer impact.

Suggested immediate items from our side: a) confirmation of root cause ownership, b) provisional credit calculation, c) change to autoscale/runbook so this doesn't repeat. Can you schedule an exec call today? Aaron (CTO) has been looped in.

Thanks,
Hanna Morris
Head of Platform Ops | Mesher

Subject: Internal: Mesher incident - quick analysis & commercial proposal (draft)

Team — quick notes after initial triage of the Mesher bundle:

Findings (initial):
- Root cause: autoscaler mis-scheduling combined with a new kernel-level memory threshold in our runtime that delayed KV cache warmup. Effect: cold-started GPU workers for a subset of routes; sustained p95/5xx across ~05:40-10:30 PT window.
- Scope: ~27% of Mesher traffic in us-west-2 affected; customer-reported window ~5 hrs matches traces.

Provisional commercial recommendation (to present to Mesher):
- One-time remediation credit = measured throughput shortfall prorated against committed monthly spend. Using their telemetry, estimate: 27% shortfall over 5 hours => equivalent to 3.1% of monthly committed tokens. Recommend a rounded credit of $85,000 as immediate remediation (covers direct customer impact and goodwill).
- Add a 60-day temporary 15% rate reduction on their routed capacity for the impacted region (to offset residual risk while we finish RCA).

Operational remediation items:
1) Rollback the recent kernel threshold change in us-west-2 and deploy a fix that forces pre-warming of the KV cache during scaling events. (Owner: Stephanie)
2) Add a policy to detect mass cold starts and auto-fallback to a warmed pool. (Owner: Ben)
3) Update our SLA calculator + billing export to show region-level credits automatically (Owner: Vivek)

Escalation asks:
- We should brief CRO and Legal on the provisional credit before sending anything externally. Vivek, can you draft the one-pager (numbers + sign-off path)?
- If Mesher requests a contract amendment (SLA addendum), loop Legal; prepare redline template.

I'll synthesize these in the external note.

— Sergio

Subject: Proposed remediation & provisional credit for Mesher incident

Hanna / Aaron —

Thanks for the call yesterday. We appreciate the level of detail in your bundle and the patience while we completed the initial internal review. Below is a concise set of next steps and the provisional commercial offer: 

What we did (summary):
- Identified autoscaler + runtime threshold interaction causing delayed KV warmup and intermittent 5xx spikes.
- Deployed a targeted rollback in us-west-2 and a hotfix that forces cache pre-warm during scale-ups; monitoring shows 95th percentile latency returning to expected range for the last 12 hours.

Provisional commercial remedy (subject to final RCA):
- One-time credit of $85,000 applied to your next invoice (reflects measured shortfall and goodwill).
- 60-day 15% temporary discount on routed capacity for affected region OR equivalent token credit, your preference.

Contract & follow-ups:
- If you want the change formalized, we can prepare an SLA addendum that documents region-level credits and a runbook-forcing pre-warm behavior. I have attached a redline-ready doc (SLA-addendum-v2.docx stub) we can iterate on.

Next steps (short timeline):
1) Mesher to confirm acceptance of provisional credit or request the alternative (discount vs. token credit) — please reply by EOD Thursday so we can queue billing.
2) Redwood will provide a completed RCA within 7 business days and a proposed SLA addendum if requested.
3) Exec call to review contract amendments if either side requests formal changes (we're happy to set that up).

Apologies again for the disruption; we want this fully remediated and documented.

— Stephanie Nguyen
SVP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
